watch_outs: The file's session_start_time, 2016-03-15, is not the recording date: the epoch names (fCamk2_201014_091141 to fCamk2_201014_122743) give 2020-10-14. Times are seconds from the first epoch's start.

The track epoch starts 22.6 s before the first position sample (7,674.30 s against 7,696.89 s), so the first 22.6 s of the epoch has spikes and no positions (epochs['track_before_tracking']); the file does not say why.

The spikes are on the position clock, not the video's: the 35 units' spatial information (compute_spatial_rates with method='binned' on this environment, the whole session) averages 0.84 bits/spike at the position timestamps, 0.36 with the positions moved 22.84 s earlier onto the video's clock, and 0.30 to 0.43 with them moved 10 or 40 s either way (checked on 2026-11-03).
The file's SleepStates score NREM during parts of the track epoch (for example 9,723 to 9,939 s, while the mouse runs along the track at 9,914 s): select running by speed, not by epochs['wake'].

The file's video timestamps are off the position clock: the video and the position series hold the same 67131 frames, and position minus video time is +22.55 to +23.12 s. The overlay shows each frame at its position sample's time; reading the video by its own timestamps puts the camera that far out of step with the positions and spikes.

The video's calibration was fitted to the tracked positions (the LED detected in the video against the file's positions), so the overlay shows the camera and the data aligned by construction: it does not check that the tracking or the declared track is placed correctly, and the track itself is not visible in the video. 90th-percentile residual 9.8 cm (84.9 px); 17.2% of LED detections are more than 5 cm off (an occluded LED or a reflection) and were left out of the fit. The lag scan's smallest median residual is at +1 to +3 frames (0.837 cm), against 0.946 cm at lag 0 (frame k with sample k): the file's position may trail the LED by 33-100 ms, so while the head moves fast the drawn position can sit behind the LED in the frame.

In the scene the video appears mirrored relative to the raw video file (for this camera, top and bottom swapped): the file's coordinates grow with the camera image's rows, downward in the image, and the scene draws y upward. The frames and the positions still agree; only the picture's orientation differs from a video player's.

Each track session interleaves "three blocks of 10 baseline runs" with "two blocks of 40 to 50 stimulation runs" (main text of Valero et al. 2022), and light unmasks place fields in non-place cells, the paper's own finding. Place fields and rate maps computed on the whole track epoch mix baseline and stimulation runs. The file's stimulus group is empty (as in 26 of the 28 files), so it holds no stimulation times and the blocks cannot be separated.

12.4% of tracked samples lie farther than half the stated 6.35 cm width from the track's centre line (the 95th percentile is 4.97 cm). This is tracking spread, not misfit: the tracked point is on the head, which swings past the edge of a narrow track and projects outward when raised. params gives no min_speed (no source read states a running threshold), so the share is not split into stopped and moving samples. The positions are kept as stored.
The file also holds UpDownStatesTimeIntervals (up and down states) and the ripples' peak times, which are not loaded; read them with pynwb.

46 runs of 11 or more identical position samples (10 or more repeats of the sample before; 2630 repeats, 3.92% of samples, 87.7 s in all, the longest 6.0 s). Positions are kept as stored. A held run is lost tracking if the tracker repeated its last fix, or the animal holding still; check before analysing stops (wells, ripples). No speed limit is stated for this dataset, so fast steps are not counted.

672 tracked position samples of 67131 (1.00%) lie outside the declared environment (env.bin_at gives -1): about 1% by construction, since the track's width was set from these samples' 99% quantile distance from the track, so the share measures neither the tracking nor the fit; params gives no min_speed, so the share is not split by speed. They are kept as stored and fall in no bin.

behavior.laps.note:
InputError: detect_laps(method='auto') counts laps around a loop, but this environment has no loop: its track graph has no cycle, or its area has no hole to run around.
Why: on a track, a tree maze or in an open arena the animal can always come back the way it went, so no lap goes round a loop and the laps found would have direction 'unknown'.
Fix: for back-and-forth runs on a linear track or arm, use detect_trials(env, times, positions, regions=[start, end]); to segment round trips against a template, pass method='reference' with reference_lap=, which reports each round trip's direction along the track as 'increasing' or 'decreasing'.

hazards.message: All 35 units are silent from 9777.5 s to 9912.2 s (135 s) while position is tracked. If the electrophysiology was not recording then, pass spike_window=(start, stop) so that time is excluded from occupancy.

bin_size=2.5 is at least the per-axis data extent [0.1651, 1.159] in every dimension.
Why: this produces very few bins, and it is often a units mistake: positions in m but bin_size meant in cm, for example.
Fix: check that bin_size and positions use the same units, then use a bin_size well below the data extent, such as bin_size=0.02

InputError: Interval filtering excluded ALL trajectory intervals (active gate(s) max_gap=1.0, min_speed=4.0).
Why: no sampling interval is left to analyse; rather than return a result in which occupancy is zero in every bin, the call refuses.
Fix: check that min_speed=4.0 is in the positions' length units per second.

InputError: Interval filtering excluded ALL trajectory intervals (active gate(s) max_gap=1.0, min_speed=4.0).
Why: no sampling interval is left to analyse; rather than return a result in which the rate map is empty, the call refuses.
